title: Preventing Outrage of Modesty Cases on MRT Trains
what_it_is: Preventing Outrage of Modesty Cases on MRT Trains

sections.label: Molestation cases on MRT trains
sections.summary: Reports of molestation on trains were 65 in 2013, 79 in 2014 and 69 last year, about 5% of annual outrage of modesty cases.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs (a) in the past three years, how many cases of molestation in MRT trains have been reported; (b) what are the plans to cut down on these cases; and (c) whether warning signs can be put up in train carriages to alert commuters.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: There were 65 cases in 2013, 79 cases in 2014 and 69 cases last year.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: These numbers have to be seen in the context of an increasing number of passenger trips on trains over the years, with almost three million passenger trips daily on trains.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The number of outrage of modesty cases on trains represent about 5% of the total number of outrage of modesty cases reported annually.

sections.label: Crime prevention messages and penalties
sections.summary: Current crime prevention messages are sufficient, no warning signs are needed, and outrage of modesty penalties are stated.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Our assessment is that the current level of crime prevention messages is sufficient and there is no need at present to include warning signs in trains.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The maximum penalty for outrage of modesty is two years' imprisonment or a fine or caning, or any combination of these punishments.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This increases to five years' imprisonment if the victim is under 14 years of age.

sections.label: Women-only carriages suggestion
sections.summary: The Government will look closely at reporting suggestions and has no plans for women-only carriages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: As for the suggestion on how to make reports and all that, it is something we will look at closely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If the number of molestation cases worsens or shows a worsening trend, would the Government consider experimenting with women-only carriages, which I think is a scheme that has met with some success in other countries?

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: There are currently no plans to have women-only carriages.
